# Getting Started with Plotly for R

[`plotly.core`](https://github.com/msummersgill/plotly.R.core) is an R package for creating interactive web-based graphs via the open source JavaScript graphing library [`plotly.js`](https://plotly.com/javascript/). Figures are built from typed graph objects (`go_figure()`, `add_scatter()`, `go_scatter_marker()`, ...) that validate every property against the plotly.js schema.

Graphs created with `plotly.core` are rendered *locally* through the [`htmlwidgets`](http://www.htmlwidgets.org/) framework.

## Installation

### Download from GitHub

`plotly.core` has not been submitted to CRAN yet. Install the development version from GitHub via the [`remotes`](https://cran.r-project.org/package=remotes) R package:

```r
remotes::install_github("msummersgill/plotly.R.core")
```

### Note For `RStudio` Users

`RStudio` users should ensure that they are using the latest [RStudio release](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/) in order to ensure compatibility with the `htmlwidgets` R package.

## Rendering Charts

By default, figures created with `plotly.core` render locally in your web browser or in the `RStudio` viewer.

```{r}
library(plotly.core)

midwest <- ggplot2::midwest

midwest |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_box(x = ~percollege, marker = go_box_marker(color = ~state))
```

Simply printing the figure object will render the chart locally in your web browser or in the `RStudio` viewer.

Graphs created with `plotly.core` are interactive!

Click on legend entries to hide/show traces, click-and-drag on the chart to zoom, double-click to autoscale, shift-and-drag to pan.

## Next Steps

Once you have installed `plotly.core`, learn more about the [structure of a figure](figure-structure.html) and start making [basic charts](bar-charts.html).
